reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended Deletion can corrupt key mappings when index removal fails and incorrectly renumber stable-ID indexes, leaving orphaned vectors.
2 open issues - [Preserve ID mapping when index removal fails](https://github.com/microsoft/semantic-kernel/pull/14702#discussion_r4433784829) · New - [Avoid renumbering IDs in indexes that preserve them](https://github.com/microsoft/semantic-kernel/pull/14702#discussion_r4433784848) · New
What changed in this PR This PR addresses #14695 by updating the Python FAISS connector’s key mappings after flat-index deletions, preventing subsequent deletes from targeting stale positions. **Changes:** - Decrement later mapped positions after each vector removal. - Add regression tests for deleting all records and maintaining correct positions after partial deletes. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `python/​tests/​unit/​connectors/​memory/​test_faiss.py` | Adds full and partial deletion regression tests. | | `python/​semantic_kernel/​connectors/​faiss.py` | Updates remaining key positions after vector deletion. |
Review effort: Balanced

I ran this on current main (df1cb33d0) and on main with this diff applied (python venv, faiss 1.15.1, real `FaissCollection`, no mocks). The diff applied cleanly.

Main reproduces the bug and it is worse than a stale count. `remove_ids` shifts later vectors down, and main kept the old positions in the key map, so the next delete in the same call or a later call removes the wrong vector. With 5 records `a` to `e`:

- `delete(["a", "b"])`: main ends with `ntotal` 3 and the map `{c: 2, d: 3, e: 4}`. The PR ends with `{c: 0, d: 1, e: 2}`.
- `delete("a")` then `delete("c")`: on main a search with `c`'s own vector returns `d`, and a search with `d`'s vector returns `b`. On the PR the surviving records `b`, `d`, `e` each find themselves.
- `delete` of all five in one call: main leaves `ntotal` at 2 with an empty map. The PR leaves `ntotal` 0.

I then checked an invariant instead of single cases. After the deletes, for every key still in the map: the vector at its list position (the order `search` uses to turn a faiss position into a key) must be that record's own vector, `ntotal` must equal the key count, and a search with the record's vector must return that record. I used 6 records and 7 delete patterns, each with one and with two vector fields:

- main breaks the invariant in 4 of the 7: `["k0","k1"]`, `"k0"` then `"k2"` (a search with `k3`'s vector returns `k1`), `["k1","k3","k4"]` (a search for `k5` raises `VectorSearchExecutionException: list index out of range`), and deleting all six.
- the other 3 are fine on main for data (deleting only the last record, deleting only `k2`, deleting `k0` twice), though the last two leave stale positions in the map.
- the PR holds the invariant in all 7, with one and with two vector fields.

Then 300 random sequences of deletes of 1 to 3 keys out of 6 records: 74 end consistent on main, 300 of 300 on the PR.

Non-flat indexes. This is a behavior change worth knowing about. With an `IndexIVFFlat` (trained), `delete("a")` on main returns without an error. Afterwards a search for `e`'s vector raises `list index out of range` and a search for `b`'s vector returns key `c`. On the PR the same `delete("a")` raises `VectorStoreOperationException: Deleting records is only supported for flat indexes ...` before anything is removed, and searches still return the right keys (`e` gives `e`, `b` gives `b`). With `IndexHNSWFlat`, main already raised (a wrapped faiss error, map left alone) and the PR raises the clearer message. So users with an IVF index who call `delete` now get an error where they used to get a silently broken index. I think that is the right call, and it may deserve a release note.

Tests. `tests/unit/connectors/memory/test_faiss.py`: 21 passed on main, 25 on the PR. If I copy the PR's test file onto main, 3 of the 4 new tests fail (`delete_multiple_keeps_index_in_sync`, `delete_updates_remaining_positions`, `delete_rejected_for_index_that_preserves_ids`). The HNSW test passes on main because main already raises there.

Limits. I did not test upserting an existing key and then deleting it, search with filters after deletes, GPU indexes, or any other index type.

Approving.

review_comments.body: If `remove_ids` raises, as it does for the accepted custom `IndexHNSWFlat`, this pop loses the key mapping while the vector and stored record remain. Retrying deletion then skips index removal and deletes only the record, leaving an orphaned vector. Read the position first and remove the mapping only after `remove_ids` succeeds.

This renumbering works for flat indexes, but accepted custom indexes such as a trained `IndexIVFFlat` preserve surviving IDs on deletion. With `a:0, b:1, c:2`, deleting `a` incorrectly remaps `b` to 0, so deleting `b` then targets a missing ID and leaves its vector behind. Renumber only indexes that compact IDs, or reject unsupported deletion semantics before mutating state, and add a stable-ID regression test.

comments.body:
Thanks, both Copilot points were valid and are addressed in the new commit:

- `_inner_delete` now calls `remove_ids` first and drops the key mapping only after it succeeds, so an index that can't remove vectors (e.g. the custom `IndexHNSWFlat`) no longer loses its mapping. Test: `test_delete_keeps_key_map_when_index_cannot_remove`.
- Only flat indexes compact ids on removal, and the key map relies on that (search resolves ids by position, upsert starts from the current count). Deleting from any other index (e.g. IVF, HNSW) now raises `VectorStoreOperationException` before anything is mutated, instead of leaving a broken mapping. Test: `test_delete_rejected_for_index_that_preserves_ids`.

Both new tests fail against the previous revision; `tests/unit/connectors/memory/test_faiss.py` passes (25 tests) and `ruff format`/`ruff check` are clean.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
